section_summary: This section records the proposed four-power division of former Japanese combat vessels of destroyer size or smaller, including the treatment of damaged ships, delivery arrangements, and vessels still needed for occupation duties. It contains draft and final diplomatic notes, ship lists, Soviet and British replies, and later correspondence about large warships and noncombatant naval craft. Several pages are duplicate copies or drafts of documents appearing elsewhere in the section.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/23, Appendix B: Analysis of Soviet reply
subfiles.about: Assesses Soviet objections to the proposed division of Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: The appendix supports allocating smaller combat vessels by four equivalent lots as ships become available and maintaining the destruction order for larger warships. It argues that Soviet requests for repatriation vessels require fuller information about existing Soviet-held ships and all military and civilian repatriation tasks.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/23, Appendix C: Proposed note to the United Kingdom, Soviet Union, and China
subfiles.to: Governments of the United Kingdom, Soviet Union, and China
subfiles.about: Proposes procedures for dividing and delivering smaller former Japanese combat vessels.
subfiles.summary: The draft provides for scrapping inoperable ships, drawing lots for four equivalent groups, and delivering available ships with Japanese crews to ports designated by the recipient governments. It anticipates later deliveries and warns that the 15 June 1946 ship lists may change.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/23, Appendix D: Proposed note to the Soviet Union
subfiles.about: Responds to Soviet proposals for a four-power commission and additional vessels.
subfiles.summary: The draft rejects a separate commission to compile ship lists because SCAP already has the information needed for division. It says initial deliveries should partly meet Soviet needs and leaves the merchant fleet's fate to later Far Eastern Commission policy decisions.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SWNCC 186/23 and SFE 182/1
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sends policy papers on Japanese combat vessels and economic concentration.
subfiles.summary: Transmits two papers for information and notes that SFE 182/1 remains unapproved.

subfiles.title: SWN-5113: Disposition of Combatant Vessels of the Japanese Navy
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Calls attention to SCAP's request while transmitting SWNCC 186/24.
subfiles.summary: Forwards SWNCC 186/24 and highlights SCAP's delivery recommendations.

subfiles.title: Department of State reply on SCAP cable C-69974
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, Department of State
subfiles.about: Provides a proposed reply to SCAP's cable about vessel division.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Department's proposed response to SCAP cable C-69974.

subfiles.title: Recommended draft message to SCAP
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Reports incorporation of SCAP's suggestion into diplomatic notes.
subfiles.summary: States that SCAP's suggestion was included in the 24 February notes to three powers.

subfiles.title: SWN-5131: Classification of proposed diplomatic notes
subfiles.about: Authorizes confidential classification for the substance of two appendices.
subfiles.summary: Allows Appendix C and D note texts to be downgraded from Top Secret to Confidential for transmission.

subfiles.title: File cover for State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee letter
subfiles.about: Identifies a letter and enclosure on Japanese combat vessels.
subfiles.summary: File cover identifies the committee letter and enclosure.

subfiles.title: SWN-5135: Request for basis of reply to SCAP
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Requests a reply to an enclosed SCAP message.
subfiles.summary: Forwards SCAP's message and asks the Department for a response.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/24: Disposition of Combatant Vessels of the Japanese Navy
subfiles.about: Circulates a SCAP message responding to earlier vessel-division policy.
subfiles.summary: Circulates SCAP's response to SWNCC 186/23 for committee information.

subfiles.title: SCAP message C-69598 on division of ex-Japanese ships
subfiles.about: Sets conditions for delivery of divided vessels.
subfiles.summary: SCAP agrees with the division policy but asks for one delivery port per government, none west of Singapore, and reimbursement for American fuel and supplies. It reports 64 ships immediately available, another 48 to follow, and demilitarization of both groups.

subfiles.title: Confidential note to Soviet ambassador on commission and merchant fleet
subfiles.about: Rejects a proposed ship-list commission and addresses Soviet vessel requests.
subfiles.summary: The United States says SCAP's ship information makes a four-power listing commission unnecessary. It expects the proposed deliveries to meet some Soviet needs and defers merchant-fleet disposition pending broader reparations and Japanese economic policy.

subfiles.title: Correction of Soviet note enclosure designations
subfiles.about: Corrects the labels of ship-list enclosures to the 24 February note.
subfiles.summary: Corrects the inoperable list to Enclosure A and the operable list to Enclosure C.

subfiles.title: Draft or duplicate note to Soviet ambassador on commission and merchant fleet
subfiles.about: Repeats the United States reply to Soviet proposals on vessel allocation.
subfiles.summary: This marked copy rejects a separate four-power ship-list commission, addresses Soviet occupation needs, and defers merchant-fleet decisions to the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Note to Soviet ambassador on division and delivery of combat vessels
subfiles.about: Explains the four-power allocation procedure for smaller Japanese combat vessels.
subfiles.summary: The note provides for scrapping unusable ships and drawing lots for four equivalent allocations. It asks for one delivery port east of Singapore, provides for Japanese crews and their return, requires reimbursement of American supplies, and reports 64 demilitarized ships ready for delivery. Further ships will follow as available.

subfiles.title: Note to British ambassador on division and delivery of combat vessels
subfiles.about: Explains the vessel-allocation procedure to Great Britain.
subfiles.summary: The British note sets out scrapping criteria, allocation by drawing lots, inspections, delivery with Japanese crews, a single port east of Singapore, and reimbursement for American supplies. It says 64 demilitarized vessels are ready for division, with further deliveries to follow.

subfiles.title: Note to Chinese ambassador on division and delivery of combat vessels
subfiles.about: Explains the vessel-allocation procedure to China.
subfiles.summary: The Chinese note sets out the same four-power drawing of lots, scrapping rules, ship inspection, delivery conditions, and reimbursement of American supplies. It requests a single Far Eastern delivery port and says 64 demilitarized vessels are ready.

subfiles.title: Enclosure A: Inoperable ex-Japanese navy ships
subfiles.about: Lists wrecked, sunk, or difficult-to-repair former Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: The inventory names destroyers, escorts, patrol craft, subchasers, minelayers, minesweepers, transports, and rescue boats classified for scrapping. It gives classes or tonnage and recorded locations across Japan.

subfiles.title: Enclosure C: Operable ex-Japanese navy ships
subfiles.about: Lists smaller former Japanese combat vessels operable within 60 days.
subfiles.summary: The inventory records destroyers, escorts, patrol and auxiliary craft, minelayers, minesweepers, cargo ships, transports, and rescue boats. Its service codes identify ships in SCAP service or minesweeping, with some locations supplied.

subfiles.title: Correction of Chinese note enclosure designations
subfiles.about: Corrects enclosure labels in the 24 February note.
subfiles.summary: Corrects the inoperable list to Enclosure A and the operable list to Enclosure C.

subfiles.title: Soviet Embassy Note No. 12
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of American ship-division notes and corrected enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Original-language note acknowledging the February notes and corrected enclosures.

subfiles.title: Translation of Soviet Embassy Note No. 12
subfiles.about: Confirms receipt of the 24 and 28 February notes.
subfiles.summary: Translation confirms receipt of the notes and their enclosures.

subfiles.title: British Embassy note on noncombatant vessels and technical data
subfiles.about: Asks how naval support craft will be treated and requests vessel specifications.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador asks about tugs, harbor craft, and salvage vessels, and requests technical details for listed transports and minesweepers.

subfiles.title: Forwarding memorandum on draft reply to British ambassador
subfiles.to: Secretary, State-War-Navy Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: Submits a draft reply to the British ambassador's 6 March note.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the proposed reply for committee consideration and action.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to British ambassador on support craft
subfiles.about: Explains exclusion of naval support craft from combatant-vessel allocation.
subfiles.summary: Says tugs, harbor craft, and salvage vessels are noncombatant; directs requests for technical data to British authorities or SCAP.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of 15 May reply to Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.about: Sends a copy of the response to the British ambassador.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the 15 May reply concerning Japanese combat vessels.

subfiles.title: Confidential file return request
subfiles.about: Requests return of a charged-out confidential file.
subfiles.summary: Asks that file 894.30/3-647 be returned to the files.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of 15 May reply to Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Sends a copy of the response to the British ambassador.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the 15 May reply concerning Japanese combat vessels.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-54 transmitting reply to British ambassador
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the American position on Japanese naval support craft.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed 15 May note says tugs, harbor craft, and salvage vessels are outside the combatant allocation and should aid Japan's economic rehabilitation. It says most are below 100 gross tons and therefore unavailable as merchant-vessel reparations, and directs requests for technical details to British records or SCAP.

subfiles.title: Unofficial translation of Soviet Embassy Note No. 14
subfiles.about: Accepts immediate vessel division and designates Nakhodka for delivery.
subfiles.summary: The Soviet Government accepts division, plans to send a representative, proposes local four-power coordination, names Nakhodka, and asks about larger warships.

subfiles.title: Copy of 24 February note to Soviet ambassador on vessel division
subfiles.about: Repeats the four-power vessel-allocation procedure.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the provisions for scrapping inoperable vessels, drawing lots for four groups, inspecting demilitarized ships, and delivering the first 64 ships. It also specifies port selection, crew return, and reimbursement for American supplies.

subfiles.title: Handwritten inquiry on interpretation of Soviet note
subfiles.about: Seeks an interpretation of Soviet proposals for the division procedure.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether Soviet representatives intend local negotiation of division details and requests comments; a routing line asks for a telephone update.

subfiles.title: Soviet Embassy Note No. 14, original
subfiles.about: Responds to the American proposal for dividing Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Original-language note corresponding to the translated Soviet acceptance and requests.

subfiles.title: Second unofficial translation of Soviet Embassy Note No. 14
subfiles.about: Repeats Soviet acceptance and requests concerning vessel allocation.
subfiles.summary: Translation accepts immediate division, names Nakhodka, proposes local coordination, and asks for information on larger warships.

subfiles.title: Department of State draft clearance note
subfiles.about: Records informal War and Navy approval of a draft.
subfiles.summary: Reports informal War and Navy approval and says committee action is unnecessary.

subfiles.title: Reply to Soviet chargé on destruction of larger warships
subfiles.about: Explains orders to destroy former Japanese warships larger than destroyers.
subfiles.summary: The reply acknowledges Soviet acceptance of the smaller-ship division and cites SCAP directives of 30 April and 6 June 1946 ordering eligible larger surface combatants destroyed. It says these ships have been or are being scrapped and directs requests for detail to SCAP in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Handwritten draft of Soviet reply opening
subfiles.about: Drafts acknowledgment of the Soviet note accepting ship division.
subfiles.summary: Draft opening acknowledges Soviet acceptance and designation of a representative.

subfiles.title: Draft note to Soviet chargé on larger Japanese warships
subfiles.about: Explains destruction of former Japanese vessels larger than destroyers.
subfiles.summary: The draft cites SCAP's 1946 directives requiring destruction of eligible large surface combatants and reports that scrapping has occurred or is under way. It refers the Soviet representative to SCAP for further details.
